expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides types.ts, api/documents.ts, useBulkSelection.ts, useDocumentMutations.ts, ConfirmDeleteDialog.tsx, Toast.tsx, BulkActionsBar.tsx, DocumentsTable.tsx

expectations.text: Produces actual working component code rather than only a list of recommendations
expectations.evidence: Full React/TypeScript implementation with hooks, grace period timer, state management, and all components

expectations.text: Makes the destructive action recoverable rather than relying on a confirmation dialog alone
expectations.evidence: Implements DELETE_GRACE_MS = 6000; mutation held behind timer; toast offers 'Undo' which calls cancelDelete to clear timeout: 'Nothing destructive happens until the grace window elapses'

expectations.text: Shows the count of affected items before the action is taken
expectations.evidence: {selectedCount.toLocaleString()} document{selectedCount === 1 ? '' : 's'} selected in bar; Delete dialog shows 'Delete {count.toLocaleString()} document{count === 1 ? '' : 's'}?' plus sampleTitles

expectations.text: Distinguishes select-all-on-page from select-all-matching rather than conflating them
expectations.evidence: Separate boolean selectAllMatching; showSelectAllBanner logic: '!selectAllMatching && allOnPageSelected && totalMatching > pageIds.length'

expectations.text: Separates the destructive action from the benign one visually or spatially
expectations.evidence: Archive and Delete buttons styled separately with distinct colors. Comment: 'Delete is spatially and visually separated from Archive so a mis-click can't slide from a benign bulk action into an irreversible one'

expectations.text: Does not make the destructive action the default focus or primary button
expectations.evidence: Delete button is secondary style (border button), not primary or focused

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No explicit statement that server must enforce rules. Mentions backend soft-delete as 'what should really be a backend...device' but does not state server enforcement responsibility.

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Closing note explicitly lists 'Made impossible (Control):' with specific examples (ambiguous selection, delete firing before grace period, header checkbox implying more than visible page, delete button clickable before phrase matches), then 'Left possible on purpose:' with explicit examples
